arena-of-death.title: Arena of Death: Heroic Combat in the Fantasy World of DragonQuest Rulebook
arena-of-death.primary_name: Arena of Death: Heroic Combat in the Fantasy World of DragonQuest
arena-of-death.primary_description: Arena of Death : Heroic Combat in the Fantasy World of DragonQuest , is a game of gladiatorial combat in a fantasy setting. The players take on the role of fighters in the arena, pitting these fighters against each other and against fearsom
headings: 1.1 Players win by increasing their character's Popularity Rating.
1.2 A Player can generate a new character if his old character dies.
1.3 Players take turns sending their characters into the arena.
1.4 Players take turns playing each other's foes.
1.5 Players may challenge each other to duels.
1.6 The order in which individual combats are resolved is determined by a random die roll.
1.7 Once a Player announces the Difficulty Factor of the foe(s) he desires to meet, his character must enter the arena.
1.8 All wounds are healed and arms and armor repaired between combats.
1.9 All members of a multi-character party must agree in advance of announcing the formation of the party who will join it and what the Difficulty Factor of its foes will be.
2.1 The Tactical Display (Side B) represents an open arena in which combat occurs.
2.2 The charts and tables printed in the rules are used to resolve various combat functions and generate combatants.
2.3 The cardboard playing pieces are used to represent individual figures and dropped or broken weapons.
2.4 The randomizer chits are used to generate random numbers necessary to the resolution of various game functions.
3.1 A Player Character's Action Point Allowance is adjusted for Agility.
3.2 A Player Character's Agility is modified by the armor the character is wearing.
3.3 A Player Character may be armed with up to 5 items from the Weapons Table and/or Shield Table.
3.4 The character's Attributes determine his capabilities in combat.
3.5 A Player Character's Manual Dexterity is affected by having a shield Prepared.
3.6 The Player's should complete a Character Record Sheet for each Player Character in the game.
5.1 A figure who flees the Tactical Display before the end of combat gains no Experience Points for the combat and suffers a loss of 3 from his Popularity Rating.
5.2 Whenever a figure (other than a monster) has 1/3 or less of his Endurance remaining, the figure's Player may ask for quarter (even if the figure, himself, is unconscious).
5.3 Any weapons which fly off the Tactical Display are considered to have flown into the crowd and to be irrevocably lost.
6.1 Figures perform Actions in order of their modified Agility.
6.2 Figures perform Actions by expending 1 or more Action Points per Action.
6.3 A figure may never expend more Action Points during a Round than he has available in his Action Point Allowance.
6.4 Figures may perform only one Action per Pulse.
6.5 Action Points may never be accumulated between Rounds or transferred between figures.
6.6 Figures must expend all of their available Action Points during a Round.
6.7 A figure may expend all of his Action Points during a Pulse.
6.8 Figures may perform only permissible Actions during a Pulse.
7.1 A figure may Move through up to 4 contiguous hexes through his Front Hexsides at a cost of 1 Action Point per hex entered.
7.2 A figure may Shift into up to 2 contiguous hexes by expending 3 Action Points to enter each hex.
7.3 A figure may Bob into up to 4 contiguous hexes by expending 2 Action Points to enter each hex.
7.4 A figure may increase the distance (in hexes) between himself and a hostile figure whose Strike Zone he occupies only by implementing a Withdraw Action.
7.5 A figure may adopt a nonstanding posture by implementing a Drop Action at a cost of 2 Action Points.
7.6 A figure may alter his posture from a lower level to a higher level by implementing a Rise Action at a cost of 4 Action Points.
7.7 A figure may change his facing without otherwise moving by implementing a Turn Action at a cost of 1 Action Point per hexside of facing changed.
7.8 A figure may Pass instead of taking some other specific Action at a cost of 2 Action Points or all of the figure's remaining Action Points (whichever is less).
8.1 A figure may Prepare a weapon for use in combat by expending 2 Action Points.
8.2 A figure may Cache a Prepared weapon in his possession by expending 3 Action Points.
8.3 A figure may Hurl a Prepared weapon at another figure at a cost of 3 Action Points.
8.4 A figure may Assail an adjacent hostile figure with his bare hands or with a Prepared weapon which is rated for use in Melee Combat at a cost of 4 Action Points.
8.5 A figure may attempt to Evade an attack of any type which may be directed against him by expending 2 Action Points.

8.6 A figure may move adjacent to a hostile figure and/or enter the hex occupied by that figure and either Assail or (if in the same hex) Grapple the figure in the same Pulse as that in which the movement was implemented by implementing a Charge Action at a cost of 4 Action Points plus the cost of any movement in which the figure engages.
8.7 A figure may Grapple a hostile figure occupying the same hex at a cost of 4 Action Points.
9.1 A figure who is not adjacent to a hostile figure may implement Actions B, C, D, E, H, M, P, Q, R, S, T and X.
9.2 A figure who is adjacent to, but not in the Attack Zone of a hostile figure may implement Actions A, B, C, D, E, H, M, P, Q, R, S, T or X.
9.3 A figure who is in the Strike Zone of a hostile figure could implement Actions A, B, D, E, H, M, P, Q, R, S, T, W or X.
9.4 A figure who occupies the same hex as a hostile figure who is conscious may employ Action E, G, P, W or X.
9.5 A stunned or unconscious figure may only implement Action X (Pass).
9.6 A figure may only attack hostile figures who occupy at least one hex of his Attack Zone.
9.7 A figure must meet all of the criteria necessary to implement an Action before he can expend Action Points to implement that Action.
10.4 Whenever a number is rolled which falls within the span given on the Special Damage Table as causing a Grievous Injury, a Grievous Injury is inflicted on the target as per 12.0.

10.5 Whenever a number is rolled which falls within the span given on the Special Damage Table as causing Damage to be subtracted from Endurance, any Damage Points inflicted on the target are automatically subtracted from Endurance instead of Fatigue.
10.6 Whenever a 99 is rolled, there is a possibility that the attacking figure has broken his weapon.
10.7 Whenever 100 is rolled, there is a possibility that the attacking figure has dropped his weapon.
11.1 A figure with 0 Fatigue Points remaining must subtract future damage from his Endurance.
11.2 Damage dice rolls of less than "1" are treated as "1."
11.3 A figure becomes "unconscious" when he has 3 or fewer remaining points of Endurance.
11.4 A figure is dead when he has no remaining Endurance.
11.5 Damage to figures may be absorbed by armor and/or shields.
11.6 A figure is "stunned" whenever he suffers a number of effective Damage Points greater than 1/3 his Endurance as a result of a single Strike.
11.7 A figure suffers a Grievous Injury whenever he is Hit and the Strike Check dice roll is within the range listed on the Special Damage Table as producing a Grievous Injury.
12.1 A figure may suffer any number of Grievous Injuries during a game.
12.2 Grievous Injuries affect Endurance (not Fatigue) and damage resulting from them is not absorbed by armor or shields.
12.3 A doubling of damage takes place after the die roll has been modified.
13.1 A figure may attack without using a weapon.
13.2 A figure may, under certain circumstances, make two attacks in the same Pulse.
13.3 Ranged Combat is only possible when the attacking figure has a weapon rated for Ranged Combat prepared and has a Line of Sight to the target he is attacking.
13.4 A figure may use a shield as a weapon.
13.5 Whenever a figure suffers a Grievous Injury or is stunned, there is a possibility that the figure will drop any weapon or shield which he holds in a prepared state.
15.1 The Difficulty Factor for a Non-Player Character is equal to the number of Experience Points divided up among the Player Characters present during combat with that Non-Player Character.

15.2 The Experience Points gained by Player Characters as a result of combat with other Player Characters is equal to two times the total PS, MD, AG, EN, FT and WP of all hostile characters involved in that combat.
15.3 Experience Points which are traded in for an increase in Attributes are never recovered.
15.4 Any Experience Points accumulated by a character who is subsequently killed are permanently lost.
